title: Katanaí watches the speech
text: In the peripheries of Katanaí, people watched the speech on televisions set up in bars and churches. When you spoke about the poor neighbourhoods, several streets in Vila Tamarin set off fireworks. The port worked normally. Local radio stations replayed the speech in the evening.

title: Katanaí watches the speech
text: In the peripheries of Katanaí, people watched the speech on televisions in bars and churches. Many had expected you to talk about the poor neighbourhoods you come from, and you did not. The reaction was quieter than the party had planned. A few local leaders told the radio they would 'wait and see'.

title: St. Veldra's financial district
text: In St. Veldra's financial district, the line about wealth 'flowing upward' was not well received. Shares in the largest banks fell slightly during the afternoon. Business associations issued short statements asking the new government for 'clarity' on taxes.

title: St. Veldra's financial district
text: In St. Veldra's financial district, the promise to reduce the burden on business was a surprise from a PM president. Shares rose slightly. The Katanaí Industrial Federation called the speech 'a promising start'.

title: St. Veldra's financial district
text: In St. Veldra's financial district, the speech was followed with attention and little reaction. Markets closed almost unchanged. Analysts said they would wait for the first budget before forming an opinion.

title: Atiaiaba
text: In Atiaiaba, the capital of Tekoku, the speech was watched by fewer people than in other cities. Your words on sovereignty were noticed. Local National Front deputies said they agreed with them and doubted you meant them.

title: Atiaiaba
text: In Atiaiaba, the capital of Tekoku, the speech was watched by fewer people than in other cities. You won few votes here. Local commentators noted that Tekoku was mentioned only briefly, and that the new cabinet has one minister from the region.

title: Sugar Bay
text: In Sugar Bay and the towns of Mognagna, where you won most of the votes, people gathered in squares to watch. Your promises about poverty and hunger were applauded. Governor Porper said the region 'expects the government to keep its word on the transfers'.

title: Sugar Bay
text: In Sugar Bay and the towns of Mognagna, where you won most of the votes, people gathered in squares to watch. The reaction was warm but cautious. Governor Porper said the region would 'wait for the budget' before celebrating.

title: Tapira
text: In Tapira, where few people voted for you, the speech was broadcast without much attention. The farmers' association said it hoped the government would 'remember who feeds the country'. The Tabernacle churches held their usual evening services.

title: Ibira
text: In Ibira, most villages have no television. The speech was heard on community radio. The Ibira Peoples' Council issued a short statement congratulating you and asking for a meeting about land rights. Governor Gaciarez attended the inauguration in person.

title: The armed forces
text: In the officers' clubs of the capital, the speech was discussed for the rest of the day. Retired officers told journalists they had hoped for a word of recognition for the armed forces. General Cazal, the Chief of Army Staff, made no comment.

title: Telegram from Arenza
text: On behalf of the people of Arenza, I congratulate you on your inauguration. Our countries have not always agreed. I hope we can meet during your term and speak frankly about the region. — Tomás Arguedas

from: Prime Minister Ottilie Varn of Veldmoor
title: Letter from Veldmoor
text: Dear President Vento, please accept the warm congratulations of the Government of Veldmoor. We value our scientific and cultural ties with Kunasai, especially with Tekoku. Our universities would welcome closer cooperation with yours. With best wishes, Ottilie Varn.

from: The Chancellery of the Archduchy of Mondrath
title: Note from Mondrath
text: The Chancellery of His Highness the Archduke of Mondrath acknowledges the inauguration of the new President of the Republic of Kunasai and conveys its formal greetings.

title: Telegram from Tarev
text: Chairman Edin Morav congratulates President Vento and expresses Tarev's wish for continued good relations along our common border, and for cooperation in trade and in the fight against crime.

title: Message from the Arennian embassy
text: President Conrad Ashby sends his congratulations to President Vento. The Federation looks forward to working with the new government on economic stability, open trade and regional security. Ambassador Lionel Pryce requests an early meeting at the President's convenience.

title: Message from the Zharani mission
text: Premier Daryun Kasrai extends his congratulations to President Vento and to the people of Kunasai. Zharan is ready to support Kunasai's development in infrastructure, ports and energy, on the basis of mutual benefit. A special envoy will be available to visit whenever the President wishes.

title: Low river at Atiaiaba
text: The harbour office at Atiaiaba reports that the Arvane river is almost two metres below its normal January level. Eleven barges are waiting to cross the sandbar at the river mouth. The office has asked for dredging.

title: Boats at night on the upper Ibira
text: Fishermen on a tributary of the upper Ibira report fast boats travelling at night without lights. They did not report it to the police. A local priest mentioned it on his radio programme.

title: A quiet river
text: Since the government's announcement on the cartels, fishermen on the upper Ibira report no boats at night. They say the smugglers are waiting to see what the government does.

title: New families above Vila Tamarin
text: A city census team counted about 1,400 families who have settled on the upper slopes above Vila Tamarin since the last harvest, most of them from Mognagna. Their houses have no sewer connection. The main sewer line of the unfinished sanitation works stops well below them.

title: Water trucks in the sertão
text: The dry season has started early in the interior of Mognagna. Governor Porper has sent water trucks to twelve towns and asked the federal government to confirm the April transfers.

title: Haze over St. Veldra
text: A brown haze has covered St. Veldra for three days. Hospitals in the old tobacco districts report more patients than usual with breathing problems.

title: Early closing in a Katanaí periphery
text: In one of Katanaí's peripheral neighbourhoods, bakeries and shops now close at four in the afternoon and buses stop at dusk. No authority ordered this. Residents say it began after blue paint marks appeared on some shop shutters, a sign associated with the Blue Piranhas.

title: Signatures in Atiaiaba
text: Volunteers in Atiaiaba are collecting signatures for Senator Lessa's proposal to distribute senators by population. They ran out of forms twice in one morning. Some of the volunteers are National Front members.

title: Irrigation pumps on the Ibira
text: Water measurements downstream suggest that new irrigation pumps on the middle course of the Ibira, in Tapira, are taking much more water than their licences allow. The state water office says the licences were issued several years ago and have not been reviewed.

title: The Jaguars' armour
text: In the palace courtyard, the Jaguar Guard's ceremonial armour is being packed into crates for the National Museum. A small crowd watched from the railings. Someone left flowers by the gate.

title: Intelligence summary (restricted)
text: Summary for the President. Foreign services: routine activity by Arennian and Zharani personnel in the capital and in Katanaí. Organised crime: the truce between the Red Tree and the Blue Piranhas holds. Evidence of informants in at least two federal offices in Ibira. Full briefing on request. — D. Kesht

title: Slowdown at the port of Katanaí
text: Dock workers at Katanaí worked strictly to the rules for one shift on Thursday, without calling it a strike. About forty ships waited at anchor until the next morning. The union said the action was about housing and transport for workers in the peripheries.

title: Survey team turned back
text: A Geological Service team sent to re-measure the Tauá Hills for the Ministry of Planning was turned back at a river crossing by armed men. Nobody was hurt. The report says the men knew the team's route in advance.

title: Rain in Sugar Bay
text: It rained in Sugar Bay for twenty minutes, the first rain since November. In the interior of Mognagna the water trucks are still running.

title: Strawberry freezes hiring
text: Strawberry, Kunasai's largest electronics company, has stopped hiring at its plant in Atiaiaba, citing uncertainty about the government's economic policy.

title: Fund mission: closing statement
text: The Fund's review mission concluded its visit to Kunasai. The mission held 'constructive discussions' with the authorities and looks forward to the government's plan for the public debt. — Anselm Royce, Head of Mission

title: Sugar Bay reacts to the budget
text: In Sugar Bay, several hundred people protested outside the federal building after the transfers were left out of the budget. Governor Porper spoke to them from the steps. He did not criticise you by name.

title: Sugar Bay reacts to the budget
text: In Sugar Bay, the renewal of the transfers was announced on local radio. Governor Porper thanked the government and asked for an emergency plan for the dry interior.

title: Letter from Veldmoor
text: Dear President Vento, the Royal Academy of Veldmoor would be glad to host twenty young Kunasaian researchers next year, if your Ministry of Education wishes. We hope they would return home afterwards. With best wishes, Ottilie Varn.

title: Shots at a police post
text: Unknown men fired at a federal police post on the upper Ibira at night. Nobody was hurt. The post had recently taken part in arrests linked to the Red Tree.

title: Boats on the river
text: Fishermen on the upper Ibira say the night traffic of fast boats has increased since the rains began. The river is higher and easier to navigate.

title: Rally for the Lessa motion
text: About twenty thousand people attended a rally in Atiaiaba in support of the Lessa motion. Senator Lessa spoke, followed by National Front leader Edvar Solano. Several speakers criticised your government.

title: Shooting in a Katanaí periphery
text: Two young men were killed in a shooting in a periphery of Katanaí. Police attribute it to the Blue Piranhas. Residents say the gang has started charging shopkeepers a weekly fee.

title: Buses to Katanaí
text: Bus companies in the interior of Mognagna have added extra services to Katanaí. Most of the passengers are families with luggage.

title: Labour talks: first round
text: The first round of talks between the Ministry of Justice, Interior and Labour and the unions took place in Katanaí. The unions asked for a minimum wage increase and transport subsidies for port workers. A second round is scheduled for August.
from: Ministry of Justice, Interior and Labour

title: Note from Tarev
text: The Government of Tarev requests that Kunasaian border units refrain from pursuing suspects across the river border, following an incident on the 14th. Tarev remains committed to joint efforts against crime.
from: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Tarev

title: A new street on the slopes
text: Families from the interior have built a new street of brick houses above Vila Tamarin in three months. The residents have named it after the town most of them came from.

title: Gold dredges on the Ibira
text: Satellite images show more than sixty illegal gold dredges on tributaries of the upper Ibira. Environmental groups say they use mercury. The dredges are believed to pay the Red Tree for protection.

title: St. Veldra and the Arenzan visit
text: Business leaders in St. Veldra welcomed President Arguedas's visit. The Katanaí Industrial Federation said a trade commission with Arenza would help exporters who 'depend too much on two large markets'.

title: Message from Vassel
text: The Government of Vassel welcomes Kunasai's proposal for talks on the Strait and will attend. We have also received the Archduchy's notice on fees.

title: Queues in the Strait
text: Shipping agents report longer waits for pilots in the Mondrathi part of the Strait. Some ships bound for Katanaí are choosing to wait for the cheaper Vassel pilots.
